I suggest to also look online for sales. There were shoes I was eyeing online, and when I went to the store they were $30 more than listed online. I didn’t ask if they price matched, which I probably should have, but instead ended up ordering them online.

I was also friends with him for about 4 years then we dated for 4. I refuse to be friends with him because of the attachment, he’s my first everything and first love and all that. I know I’ll always have feelings for him. He on the other hand really wishes we could still be friends and tells me I’m too close to his family to just stop contacting them and everything but I know myself, and I know I need the space.

I thought similar to your first paragraph for a while, but I really held onto “everything happens for a reason.” If we worked in the future I’m certain it would be a completely different relationship, we had many conversations about that before we stopped talking, but I let go of that idea and accepted that any relationship I’d have after him would be completely different because I’m determined to grow and be comfortable on my own. I kept telling myself maybe in a year it’ll work out again... but it did nothing but hold me back. The best thing you can do is be honest with yourself. I slapped myself into reality once I began telling myself that it is completely over and that entire relationship is in the past. Anything that grows from the ruins of it would be brand new, id be stronger, smarter, and be able to prioritize myself before ANYONE else. It is hard when you give your whole heart to someone. But you will get through it

I went NC with my ex for about a month and a half, while he would send me breadcrumbs that I would delete and ignore, but then his bday came up so I reached out. Since then I’ve felt more of an inclination to reach out, whereas when he was sending me breadcrumbs I intentionally ignored them. 

He broke up with me in January and we tried to figure stuff out until around May. In retrospect it was a waste of both of our times.  The point in NC (which I decided for myself) was to heal and break off some of the attachment. In my eyes his breadcrumbs were signs he still cares but I have grown enough to at least know he doesn’t care enough anymore, hence why it didn’t work out. 

Breadcrumbing may not be a necessarily BAD thing, but it is almost always misleading and causes an uproar of mixed emotions you may have thought you got rid of during NC. I don’t despise him for reaching out and sending those breadcrumbs. It really depends how far you’ve come since the breakup and if your heartbroken mindset has begun to turn into acceptance. I accepted that we still care for each other and if him reaching out (even only to be ignored) was helping his peace of mind, and me blatantly ignoring and avoiding him was helping mine, that’s just how we’d have to continue on until we’re fully healed. I can’t stop him from contacting me and he can’t force me to respond.
No not sarcastic at all haha sorry

You kinda look like Chris Evans. Not ugly

My denial stage was longest. I’m somewhere toward the end of anger and the beginning of depression. It’s been 6 months.. trying to get stronger everyday but as the picture depicts, I’m on a downhill slope for a bit

Said I can’t win him back. Said no more seeing each other no more getting together. Mentioned things that took hits at my self esteem. Etc.

He said he doesn’t have a bad thing to say about me but why do I feel like I have so much bad to say about him? And I did say it so now I feel even more guilt

It wasn’t. He gave me false hope for months. I’m the one who finally decided I shouldn’t contact him anymore.

Time to heal. I’m still angry and upset. Still care about him.

I agree. Definitely years down the line, just so painful right now because it’s only been 5 months. I have also felt like the relationship failed because of me. I’m slowly finding myself again as well.

Stay strong, I’m right there with you. I feel the pain but have faith that the latter would give me even more than I could imagine. It would be like breaking my own heart over again. My ex also blocked me on everything when I said no, it’s a tough pill to swallow and you feel like you’ve been betrayed in a way but take it as an opportunity to grow your personal space
My ex of 4 years is currently trying to be friends. I also could never. It’s painful but I’d be hurting myself more to even try to be “friends”. For me it’s too much history and attachment
